text:
sara-ng: FYI I saw a tail-latency blip on canary after turning on coalesced batching + paged-KV paging hints. Numbers below, need quick triage :eyes:

mike-k: Ugh. Which canary? dedicated-gpu-3?

sara-ng: dedicated-gpu-3, flashv2 path. Baseline (no coalesce/paging): p95 ~ 28ms. With coalesced batching + aggressive KV page prefetch it jumps to p95 ~ 44ms and p99 ~ 210ms. avg little changed.

jordan-b: Do you have flamegraphs or kernel selection logs? My money's on the kernel selector flipping to fusedFlash for some seq lengths and that path not being friendly to paged KV working set.

sara-ng: attaching the quick sampling I pulled from the deploy logs: 

bench-bot: ```
kernel_select: input_len=1024, kv_pages=18, chosen_kernel=FlashAttnV2
kernel_select: input_len=2048, kv_pages=36, chosen_kernel=FusedAttentionLegacy
kv_pager: page_faults=12/60s, cold_pages=5
batch_coalescer: merged_requests=3-7, avg_coalesced_seq=768
latency_samples: 95th=44.3ms, 99th=209.7ms
```

lee-zhang: Interesting. So selector is switching to FusedAttentionLegacy for longer inputs. That fused path expects contiguous KV in GPU memory, right? If paging causes more scatter, it might thrash.

anya: Also check the block-table eviction pattern. If blocks are being moved mid-request due to our reactive allocator, we could get stalls. Any compaction runs at the same time?

mike-k: We did a background compaction job on that pool around 03:14 UTC (auto-defrag). Could line up. Need to see allocator logs: slab vs hybrid fallback events.

sara-ng: grabbed allocator trace from same window: 

bench-bot: ```
alloc_strategy: hybrid
slab_alloc_failures: 4
fallback_to_heap: true
block_table_relocs: 3
pager: on_demand_prefetch=true, coalesce_hint=true
page_coalescer: coalesced_writebacks=9
```

jordan-b: slab_alloc_failures + relocations is a red flag. If block table entries are being relocated while KV cache lookups happen, the kernel may stall waiting on remote page fetches. That would amplify p99.

lee-zhang: Could be our race: coalescer reads sequence of requests, triggers kernel_select for the merged batch, then allocator decides to move some pages to satisfy larger contiguous slab, causing in-flight remap. We should ensure allocator doesn't relocate hot pages during an active batch.

anya: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: make relocations defer until no active inflight batches on that shard, or mark hot pages pinned for the duration of kernel submission.

mike-k: We can try a conservative selector rule: prefer FlashAttnV2 if pager cold_pages > threshold or if slab_alloc_failures > 0. FlashAttnV2 appears to be more tolerant of scattered KV because it uses chunked loads.

sara-ng: I ran a quick experiment toggling that heuristic on one canary and tail dropped back: p95 ~ 30ms, p99 ~ 82ms. Not perfect but much better.

jordan-b: Nice. Can we get a micro-bench showing memory access patterns? Maybe instrument block-table lookup histogram per kernel.

bench-bot: ```
microbench: kernel=FlashAttnV2, seq=1024, kv_page_reads=210, gpu_mem_reads=1.2M
microbench: kernel=FusedAttentionLegacy, seq=2048, kv_page_reads=420, gpu_mem_reads=2.4M
page_latency: avg_pull=2.8ms, tail_pull=28ms (when cold_pages>3)
```

lee-zhang: Those pull tail numbers look like page fault on demand IO causing the long stalls. Our pager does async prefetch but if coalesced batch increases effective working set suddenly we outrun prefetch.

anya: Two possible routes: 1) throttle coalescing to limit peak working set per batch, 2) improve prefetch heuristics to look at upcoming sequences in coalesced batch and prefetch their pages, or 3) pin hot blocks during batch as said earlier.

mike-k: We should also add a selector signal 'estimated_kv_working_set' computed from coalesced_seq distribution and block_table residency to avoid picking fused kernels that assume contiguity.

sara-ng: Actionable plan: 
- revert heuristic in production to prefer FlashAttnV2 when pager cold_pages>2 (temp) (mike)
- add allocator guard to avoid relocating blocks with active inflight batches (lee)
- add telemetry for block-table lookup histogram and kernel selection reasons (jordan)
- adjust prefetch to inspect coalesced batch addresses (anya)

mike-k: I'll push a canary with the selector change in 15m.

lee-zhang: I'll prototype a 'pin-for-submission' flag on block entries — cheap reference count increment at batch submit and decrement on completion. If it's 0 we allow relocation.

jordan-b: I'll wire up a dashboard: per-kernel p95/p99, allocator fallbacks, reloc counts, cold_page_count and coalesced_batch_size.

anya: If we do pinning, ensure we don't deadlock compaction. Compaction should respect pin counts and skip pinned blocks; compaction backpressure might be needed.

sara-ng: Thanks everyone. Once canary is up I'll report back with numbers. For the writeup later let's capture the failing scenario and the root cause hypothesis: coalesced batching increased instantaneous KV working set which, combined with allocator relocations and reactive prefetch, caused fused kernel to encounter long cold pulls leading to tail latency.

bench-bot: canary-deploy: selector-heuristic-toggle -> deployed to dedicated-gpu-3 at 03:42 UTC

mike-k: Canary looks good after fix: p95 29ms, p99 88ms (stable for 12m). I'll promote to the pool if stable for 30m. :thumbsup:

sara-ng: Great. Will follow up with a short postmortem + checklist for future kernel+pager changes.

lee-zhang: Filing follow-up RFC for allocator pinning + compaction semantics.

jordan-b: Adding a regression test in perf-suite that simulates coalesced batches + constrained slab to catch this earlier.

anya: Nice. Thanks all.

sara-ng: closing the loop :white_check_mark:
